title: The Shanghai Sunday Times April 6, 1924

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, APRIL 6, 1924.
LUNGWHA AEROPLANES SENT
TO HANGCHOW
Concentrated Training Away From
The Foreigner's Eyes
MACHINES' BOMBING APPARATUS
Defenceless Position Of Shanghai Now More
Serious ; Foreign Pilots Engaged
By "Spad".
It was the late Lord Northcliffe who, at a squadron reunion dinner in 1920, stated that our hope of he future lies in the air. It may also be said that Great Britain and her associate nations—Australia, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa and India—have in their services the best flying men in the world, who, backed by the mother country's skilled mechanics and business men, may be relied upon, if properly encouraged by the public, to maintain for us the same place in the air that we have held at sea for so many centuries.
Apathy In Britain
At the annual reunion dinner recently held by the Shanghai ex-R. A. F. members, the Chairman made some very pertinent remarks on the apathy that is shown by Great Britain towards aviation today, of the great struggle made by the Royal Air Force to be recognized as a separate and not as an auxiliary service. He touched on the supineness of the sister services, which has made the problem more difficult, of how the R. A. F. through its own efforts has now come to be recognized as a third branch of the forces, carrying its own blue ensign.
Neither Navy nor Army can today be efficient without an Air Force. The recent announcement that the Home Defence Squadrons are to be expanded by an additional 400 flying officers and the creation of a Territorial Air Force, gives us food for thought in Shanghai. Locally we are without any possible means to repel attacks from the air, and the importation of aeroplanes into China during the past year can only bring us to the conclusion that our defence schemes have to be radically revised. In previous articles published locally only the very fringe of the subject which is causing such intense interest in practically all the European countries, has been touched upon, yet China is not different in this respect from any other nation.
Pilots For Chinese Machines
The writer is not prepared to face the limelight of publicity on the defence schemes of the Settlement. He would answer
the argument by taking the proposition that strategy is all one, and saying that there must be no risk of an independent sea or land service devising "unrelated theories," inasmuch as it is admitted by every authority that the air power must in any scheme of offence or defence exert a decisive effect on the cause of the campaign.
Thanks to the publicity given in these columns, the military aviation activity of the many Tuchuns is well known. What is not so commonly known is that these machines are being manned by European pilots, and the transference of the Lunghwa Aerodrome to Hangchow has a significance that only those in authority can gauge. These machines are not only intended to do the usual aerial reconnaissance and fighting, but a great number are fitted up with bomb racks of the latest improvements, with electrical apparatus, wireless and bomb sights.
Protection of Trade
It is not my purpose, fortunately, to write here of war; but as a student of aerial power from its early days, I do feel that we should all realize that a defence policy based upon aircraft affords us the only hope of protecting our trade out here. In the war from which we have just emerged the offensive and destructive powers of aircraft were little more than foreshadowed. It was, in a sense, a mere warning to the world—a warning of what may be possible in the future, and in the not very distant future, if this power of navigating the air, and of building larger and more powerful machines, is turned again to the work of destruction. China to-day has imported machines fitted with bombing equipment and apparatus of the 1918 pattern. Her arsenals are as good as any of the emergency ones of the war, and the matter of making bombs of all calibres is much less difficult than to harness the pony teams to the local guns.
Aeroplanes can carry high explosive and incendiary bombs for the destruction of material, and although the results obtainable in the war were limited, first by the

龙华飞机被送往杭州
集中训练以避开外国人耳目
飞机的轰炸装置
上海目前毫无防备的局势更为严峻；“斯帕德”公司雇佣外籍飞行员。
已故的诺思克利夫勋爵（Lord Northcliffe）曾在1920年的一次中队重聚晚宴上表示，我们未来的希望在于空中。也可以说，大不列颠及其附属国——澳大利亚、加拿大、新西兰、南非和印度——在其服役人员中拥有世界上最优秀的飞行员，在母国熟练机械师和商人的支持下，如果得到公众的适当鼓励，可以信赖他们为我们保持在空中的地位，就像我们在海上保持了许多世纪的地位一样。
英国的冷漠态度
在最近举行的上海前皇家空军成员年度重聚晚宴上，主席就英国当今对航空表现的冷漠态度，以及皇家空军为被承认为一个独立兵种而非辅助兵种所做出的巨大努力，发表了一些非常切中要害的言论。他提到了其他军种的懈怠，这使得问题更加困难，即皇家空军如何通过自身努力，如今已被承认为军队的第三分支，并拥有自己的蓝色军旗。
如今，没有空军，海军或陆军都无法有效运作。最近宣布本土防御中队将增补400名飞行军官，并建立一支本土空军，这令我们在上海深思。在本地，我们没有任何可能的手段来抵御来自空中的攻击，而过去一年飞机输入中国的情况只能让我们得出结论：我们的防御计划必须进行根本性的修订。此前在本地发表的文章仅触及了那个在几乎所有欧洲国家引起极大兴趣的话题的边缘，然而中国在这方面与其他国家并无不同。
为中国飞机配备飞行员
笔者不准备面对公众关注租界防御计划的 spotlight（焦点）。他将通过接受“战略是一体的”这一命题来回答这一论点，并指出，绝不能让独立的海军或陆军部门制定“无关的理论”，因为所有权威人士都承认，在任何进攻或防御计划中，空中力量必须对战役进程产生决定性影响。
得益于本报专栏的宣传，许多督军的军事航空活动已广为人知。但不太为人所知的是，这些飞机由欧洲飞行员驾驶，而龙华机场迁往杭州具有只有当局才能估量的意义。这些飞机不仅旨在进行常规的空中侦察和战斗，而且大量飞机配备了最新改进型的炸弹架、电气装置、无线电和瞄准具。
保护贸易
幸运的是，我在此无意谈论战争；但作为一名从早期就开始研究空中力量的学生，我确实感到我们都应认识到，基于飞机的防御政策是我们在这里保护贸易的唯一希望。在我们刚刚结束的战争中，飞机的进攻和破坏能力仅仅初露端倪。从某种意义上说，这只是对世界的一个警告——警告如果在未来，且在不太遥远的将来，这种驾驭天空以及建造更大、更强力机器的能力再次被用于破坏工作，可能会出现什么情况。中国今天进口的飞机配备了1918年款式的轰炸设备和装置。她的兵工厂与战时任何应急兵工厂一样好，而且制造各种口径炸弹的难度远小于将小马队套在当地的大炮上。
飞机可以携带高爆炸弹和燃烧弹以破坏物资，尽管战争中取得的效果受到限制，首先是因

secondly by the difficulty of drop-
ping bombs accurately, to-day
sustained and systematic attacks
can be made with a much great-
er accuracy than any battery, or
for that matter battleship guns,
can possibly expect to do when
shooting for destruction of
material, and at far less cost. It
is a well known fact that batteries
were allowed 400 rounds of am-
munition to destroy an enemy 4-
gun battery. Compare this with
an airman's six bombs allotted for
a similar task. How vast an im-
provement has been made with
bombing machines and bombs may
be understood when we know
that it took just two minutes
in one case and four minutes in the
other to sink two ships of the
Dreadnought class, and forty
bombs were dropped.
4,000 lb. Bomb
We have to-day bombing planes
of a wing spread of 123 feet, with
a petrol tank of 2,150 gallons,
mounting 7 machine guns and
carrying a bomb or bombs to the
vast extent of 12,000 pounds, and a
cruising radius of 2,000 miles. The
usual one in use at the moment
is the 4,600-pound demolition
bomb, with nose and tail fuses
loaded with approximately 2,000
pounds of T. N. T., and is 13
feet long. The body consists of a
steel drum 23 inches in diameter.
The effect of such a bomb drop-
ping, say, in Nanking Road, may
be realized when it is known that
when striking earth the bomb
throws a cloud to a height of more
than a thousand feet, and makes
a crater averaging over 70 feet
in diameter, with, if fitted with a
delay fuse, a depth of over 20
feet. There is no reinforced con-
crete building in Shanghai that
could resist this bomb, or for that
matter one a quarter its size. It
is not a difficult job for the aver-
age machine we have seen flying
around Shanghai to load with 600
pounds, but there are greater ones
in China, and even a 600-pound
bomb would make a nasty mess of
the Hongkong Bank.
Local Machines
Things are moving fast, and it
is fairly obvious that the Chinese
military Tuchun has recognized
the value of the bomb-dropping
machine. Of a recent inspection
carried out by the writer of over
30 machines of all types, every
one was fitted with bomb racks
and equipment complete, and it
must always be remembered that
very little skill is required from
the pilot when dropping bombs on
targets of large area--just the
rapid use of sights will give
sufficiently accurate results. It
is not suggested that the object
of the military Tuchun in fitting
up his aeroplanes with bombs is
to destroy cities or treaty ports;
he is, possibly, only concerned
with destroying enemy railways
and guns, but the possibilities of
such a potent weapon of warfare,
more especially when there is no
method of defence against it,
must not be overlooked.
It is Marshal Foch who com-
plains that it is the habit of the
military mind to think of the
next war in terms of the last. All
our defence schemes are worked
out from this angle. We continue
to train the army in the light of
the lessons learnt during the last
great struggle. Yet, who shall
say how this army is to be em-
ployed when next it takes the
field? Who shall say that our
local Volunteers will manoeuvre
similarly to the 1913 riots even?
Will the gunners be safe behind
their gun shield? Will the gun-
boats be able to carry out their
shelling without trouble? The
writer suggests that the answer is
an emphatic "No."
Terrible Possibilities
There are many uses for the
aeroplane, not the least being
photography. Imagine the subtle
move of the solitary airman who
comes over at daybreak at a great
height, circles the Race Course,
and goes quietly away. Who
could have connected such an
event with the shelling the battery
received ten minutes later? But
the more forceful effort of the
plane that arrived at 10 a.m. and
dropped a bomb right on G. H. Q.
would be thoroughly understood
by the Navy and Army alike.
However, there is a more deadly
enemy even than the high ex-
plosive bomb, and that is the
plane using gas bombs. It will
assuredly be the most deadly
enemy we shall have to face. The
rifle, bayonet, and machine gun
are conventional equipment of
slaughter, but become impotent
and an encumbrance against gas.
Long before the Chinese import-
ed machines in such numbers as
they have done in the last year,
the writer had an interview one
day with a very distinguished
army officer who was in Shanghai.
The topic of conversation was
what might be done with aircraft
if a real air policy could be adopt-
ed in the defence scheme of
Shanghai, and the writer would
like to record the fact that this
officer had, by the end of the
talk, grasped completely the idea
of air power in its widest applica-
tion, but it did not enter into the
defence scheme. Unfortunately,
as in so many other cases, here
the matter ended. The fact, how-
ever, remains, that what was con-
sidered then as highly improbable,
was a fact in less than three
months after that officer left
Shanghai, for machines were being
imported by the Chinese.
The writer knows he will be
told of a hundred and one other
obstacles which stand in our path.
But these obstacles are not insur-
mountable.
Why Aerodrome Was Moved
The Chinese have aeroplanes of
the most modern design. No-one
can deny this. They have found
no dearth of pilots. They have
moved the local aerodrome to get
a greater concentration of train-
ing away from the prying eyes of
the foreigner. They have fitted
many machines with bombing ap-
paratus. They have been search-
ing for a gas chemist, and, finally,
they have turned down commercial
aviation for aerial warfare. Does
anyone suggest, in face of these
facts, that the S. V. C. will never
have to do more than contend with
ordinary street riots that the
police would deal with, or that the
gunboats offer us complete pro-
tection?
It is no good bewailing the past.
What is done is done. Our main
interest, now, is to see what
lessons the past teaches, and how
we can profit by these lessons in
the future.
Here the writer knows he is
verging upon wide and debatable
ground. To many people there is
something peculiarly galling in
being told, just as they are draw-
ing breath after the mighty
struggle from which we have
emerged, that they must gird up
their loins and be prepared, and
that we should not turn our backs
for one moment on the idea that
we may be caught napping in the
S. V. C. by a sudden and unpleas-
ant surprise.

为载重能力小，
其次是因为准确投掷炸弹的
困难，但如今可以进行持续
且系统的攻击，其准确度远
高于任何炮台，或者就此而
言，战舰火炮在射击以破坏
物资时可能达到的水平，且
成本低得多。众所周知的事
实是，为了摧毁敌方一个四
门炮的炮台，允许炮台消耗
400发弹药。将此与飞行员执
行类似任务所分配的六枚炸
弹进行比较。当我们得知在
一种情况下仅用两分钟，另
一种情况下用四分钟就击沉
了两艘无畏级（Dreadnought class）
战舰，且投下了四十枚炸弹
时，就可以理解轰炸机和炸
弹取得了多么巨大的进步。
4,000磅炸弹
今天我们拥有翼展123英尺
的轰炸机，油箱容量2,150加
仑，装有7挺机枪，并可携带
重达12,000磅的一枚或多枚
炸弹，巡航半径为2,000英里。
目前常用的炸弹是4,600磅的
爆破炸弹，其头部和尾部引
信装填了约2,000磅T.N.T.炸
药，长13英尺。弹体由一个直
径23英寸的钢制圆筒组成。
当人们知道炸弹击中地面时
会扬起一千多英尺高的尘云，
并形成一个平均直径超过70
英尺、若配备延时引信则深
度超过20英尺的弹坑时，就
可以想象这样一枚炸弹落在
南京路等地所产生的效果。
上海没有任何钢筋混凝土建
筑能够抵御这种炸弹，甚至
连其四分之一大小的炸弹也
无法抵御。对于我们在上海
周围看到的普通飞机来说，
装载600磅并非难事，但中国
还有更大的飞机，即使是一
枚600磅的炸弹也会把汇丰银
行（Hongkong Bank）炸得一塌
糊涂。
本地飞机
事态发展迅速，显然中国军
事督军已经认识到投弹飞机
的价值。在笔者最近检查的
30多架各型飞机中，每一架
都配备了完整的炸弹架和设
备，并且必须始终记住，在
对大面积目标投掷炸弹时，
对飞行员的技术要求很低——
只需快速使用瞄准具即可获
得足够准确的结果。并非指
出军事督军为其飞机配备炸
弹的目的是摧毁城市或条约
口岸；他可能只关心摧毁敌
方的铁路和大炮，但这种强
大战争武器的可能性，特别
是在没有任何防御方法的情
况下，不容忽视。
福煦元帅（Marshal Foch）曾
抱怨，军事思维的习惯是用
上一场战争的思路来思考下
一场战争。我们所有的防御
计划都是从这一角度制定的。
我们继续根据上次大战中吸
取的教训来训练军队。然而，
谁能说下次这支军队投入战
场时将如何部署？谁能说我
们本地的万国商团（Volunteers）
会像1913年骚乱时那样进行
演习？炮手们在炮盾后面会
安全吗？炮艇能够顺利执行
炮击任务吗？笔者建议，答
案是明确的“不”。
可怕的可能性
飞机有许多用途，摄影至少
是其中之一。想象一下，一
名孤独的飞行员在黎明时分
从高空飞来，绕跑马厅盘旋
一圈，然后悄然离去。谁能
将这一事件与十分钟后炮台
遭受的炮击联系起来呢？但
上午10点到达并直接在总司
令部（G. H. Q.）投下一枚炸
弹的飞机所造成的更强烈的
冲击，海军和陆军都能充分
理解。
然而，还有一种比高爆炸弹
更致命的敌人，那就是使用
毒气弹的飞机。这无疑将是
我们必须面对的最致命的敌
人。步枪、刺刀和机枪是常
规的杀戮装备，但在毒气面
前变得无能为力且成为累赘。
早在中国人像过去一年那样
大量进口飞机之前，笔者曾
有一天采访了一位在上海的
非常杰出的陆军军官。谈话
的主题是，如果上海的防御
计划能采取真正的空中政
策，利用飞机会做些什么，
笔者想记录这样一个事实：
这位军官在谈话结束时完全
掌握了空中力量在最广泛应
用中的概念，但这并未纳入
防御计划。不幸的是，正如
在许多其他情况下一样，事
情到此为止。然而，事实依
然存在，当时被认为极不可
能的事情，在该军官离开上
海后不到三个月就成了现
实，因为中国人正在进口飞
机。
笔者知道，人们会告诉他道
路上还有一百零一个其他障
碍。但这些障碍并非不可逾
越。
为何迁移机场
中国人拥有设计最现代的飞
机。这一点无人能否认。他
们并不缺乏飞行员。他们迁
移了本地机场，以便在避开
外国人窥探视线的情况下进
行更集中的训练。他们为许
多飞机配备了轰炸装置。他
们一直在寻找一位气体化学
家，最后，他们放弃了商业
航空而转向空中战争。面对
这些事实，还有人建议说，
万国商团（S. V. C.）永远只
需应对警察会处理的普通街
头骚乱，或者炮艇能为我们
提供全面保护吗？
哀叹过去无济于事。木已成
舟。我们现在的主要兴趣在
于看看过去教给我们什么教
训，以及我们如何在未来从
这些教训中受益。
在此，笔者知道他正涉足广
泛且有争议的领域。对许多
人来说，就在我们从刚刚结
束的巨大斗争中喘口气之
际，却被告知必须整装待
发，做好准备，并且我们绝
不能片刻忽视这样的想法：
万国商团可能会因突然且不
愉快的意外袭击而措手不及，
这种感觉尤其令人恼火。

AIR FLEETS OF THE TUCHUNS
S. Times
PILOTS AND INSTRUCTORS 20-1-24.

What The Importation Of Cavalry Tanks
Means To Shanghai

A SIGNIFICANT OFFICIAL OMISSION

By "CONTACT"

Know this, my brethren, Heaven is clear
And all the clouds are gone—
The Proper Sort shall flourish now,
Good times are coming on—
The evil text was threatened late
To all of our degree,
Hath passed in discord and debate,
And, Hey then up go we!

RUDYARD KIPLING.
* * *

Until the late summer of 1922, flying, in any of its forms, by airship or aeroplane, was looked upon by the vast majority of folk either as some new weapon of modern warfare—fascinating or terrible as the case might be—or as an up-to-date form of Roman gladiator exhibition in which, under very dangerous conditions, our youth risked life and limb to make a public holiday.

Rapid Development

Aviation and airmanship are at present in their veriest infancy. The man in the street knows flying only as a feature of modern war. He realizes that it owes its swift development to war conditions. But he would doubtless be very surprised to learn that, in the course of the five years since the Armistice, the technique of aviation and its attendant uses have developed even more rapidly than during the five years of war.

To-day we see the Royal Air Force recognized as a separate and distinct service, with its own ensign. We see our Colonies following the policy that war strength in the air must necessarily depend upon commercial air strength, both in personnel and material. We read of a daily service from London to Moscow. We expected to see a commercial service from Shanghai to Harbin, thence Harbin to Moscow, and so linking Shanghai to London direct.

Plaything Of Chinese War Lords

But no; the extravagant civil aviation plans of the Aeronautical Bureau of the Chinese Government have vanished in thin air; the immense sums of money spent on aerodromes by the Central Government have been wasted, and the Bureau itself has become the plaything of the war-lords.

"There can be no commercial aviation in China until there is a Government to guarantee safety of property and to encourage foreign capital to invest in Chinese enterprises. In the meantime, aeroplanes have become the plaything of the war lords, each striving to obtain supremacy. Not a single one of these Tuchuns wishes to encourage commercial aviation, in fact, they have completely neutralized such efforts by the simple process of refusing to place their seal to the documents granting landing facilities, and despite the fact that General Lu has made an aerial compact with Marshal Chang, facilities for landing at Tientsin and Mukden have been refused, and Peking has no power to interfere in either case."

Why Tuchuns Have Planes

These Tuchuns are providing themselves with aeroplanes solely for the purpose of making war. Camouflaging their efforts as much as possible, one only recently went to the extent of publishing in the foreign Press a letter to the effect that he was not in the market to purchase machines from foreign concerns, but he omitted to add that he had facilities to purchase elsewhere. Yet another loudly proclaimed, through similar channels, that he would not make war, wished for peace, and was determined to keep the peace. At the same time he is frantically importing aeroplanes and cavalry tanks to outstrip a near neighbour. But aeroplanes are useless without pilots, and it will be interesting to watch where the Tuchuns obtain their men.

Marshal Chang's Fleet

So far as can be ascertained, Marshal Chang has the largest air fleet in China. He received 40 French aeroplanes on December 6, previously described in these columns and erroneously reported by Reuter's as 12. At that time he had about 30 serviceable machines, with about 90 engines and parts from Italy, so he has actually a fleet of 60 war and 40 school bases. Civil aviation now being closed down, the last remaining British instructor has left, but Marshal Chang still retains eight Russian pilots, and is getting a fresh lot of Chinese together. He is expecting a delivery of six small tanks.

Marshal Wu Pei-fu has about 30 serviceable machines at Lo-yang with several good pilots.

Machines At Nanyuan

President Tsao Kun has about 40 serviceable machines at Nanyuan. They include the Avro, Vimys, and Handley Pages. He employs an American instructor, one foreign rigger and one foreign fitter, and about 20 Chinese pilots. About three months ago Tsao presented two machines to the Tuchun at Nanking, who had the military parade ground there turned into an aerodrome. Dr. Sun has about 11 machines with some Chinese pilots. And it is rumoured that all of these Tuchuns are frantically buying truck chassis to make armoured cars.

Gen. Ho's Armoured Cars

General Ho Feng-ling has 25 French machines and two others, all of which have been described in these columns. He has one Chinese pilot, two under-instructors and one foreign pilot, with 12 French cavalry tanks. If these Tuchuns, and the writer says "if" advisedly, can train pilots or obtain pilots, then serious trouble is inevitable. There will be no such thing as a neutral zone in the airmen.

The Washington Conference, like the League of Nations remains a nine days' wonder. With a gesture which was magnificent, governments gave their battleships, built and building, to the scrap heap. When the peoples had had time to recover from their astonishment at such a remarkable act of self-denial they realized the cynicism of it. The battleships were scrapped because, in face of aircraft, they were obsolete and valueless. And lest there should remain any lingering doubts on the subject, it may be said that Japan is spending as much on aircraft as Great Britain is to-day. America is also building up a huge air fleet involving the establishment of 2,500 officers and 40,000 other ranks. Whilst the three countries mentioned are building the largest aircraft armies the world has ever seen, presumably China is attempting, in her disjointed way, to place military aviation on a sound basis.

The S. V. C.

Yet we here are still slow to learn, and if we are to judge by the present attitude of the S.V.C. towards aviation, we are content to ignore the lesson so bitterly learnt, and even before the ink is dry on this paper our armoured cars have found their master.

一项意味深长的官方疏漏

作者：“CONTACT”

须知，我的弟兄们，天已晴朗，
乌云散尽——
正派之人如今将兴旺发达，
好日子即将来临——
那曾威胁我们要命的邪恶文本，
已在一团混乱与辩论中过去，
嘿，于是我们振作起来！

鲁德亚德·吉卜林（Rudyard Kipling）。
* * *

直到1922年夏末之前，绝大多数民众看待任何形式的飞行，无论是飞艇还是飞机，要么将其视为现代战争的一种新式武器——视情况而定，既迷人又可怕；要么将其视为一种时髦的罗马角斗士表演，在这种表演中，我们的青年在极其危险的条件下冒着生命危险和肢体伤残的风险，只为给公众假期增添娱乐。

快速发展

航空业和飞行技术目前仍处于真正的萌芽阶段。普通市民对飞行的了解仅限于它是现代战争的一个特征。他意识到，其迅速发展归功于战争环境。但他无疑会非常惊讶地得知，在停战后的五年里，航空技术及其相关用途的发展速度甚至比战争期间的五年还要快。

今天，我们看到皇家空军被承认为一个独立且独特的军种，拥有自己的军旗。我们看到我们的殖民地遵循这样的政策：空中战争力量必然取决于商业航空力量，无论是在人员还是物资方面。我们读到有关从伦敦到莫斯科的每日航班服务的报道。我们曾期待看到从上海到哈尔滨，再从哈尔滨到莫斯科的商业航班服务，从而将上海与伦敦直接连接起来。

中国军阀的玩物

但是，事实并非如此；中国政府航空局的宏大民用航空计划已化为泡影；中央政府在机场建设上花费的巨额资金已被浪费，而该局本身已成为军阀们的玩物。

“在中国没有一个能保障财产安全并鼓励外资投入中国企业的政府之前，就不可能有商业航空。与此同时，飞机已成为军阀们的玩物，每个人都力求获得 supremacy（霸权/优势）。这些督军中没有一个人希望鼓励商业航空，事实上，他们通过简单地拒绝在授予着陆设施的文件上盖章，完全抵消了此类努力。尽管卢将军与张元帅达成了空中协定，但在天津和沈阳的着陆设施仍被拒绝，而北京方面在这两种情况下均无权干涉。”

督军为何拥有飞机

这些督军为自己配备飞机纯粹是为了进行战争。尽可能掩饰他们的努力，其中一人最近甚至在外国报刊上发表了一封信，大意是他不打算从外国公司购买机器，但他省略了补充说明他有能力从其他地方购买。另一人则通过类似渠道大声宣称，他不会发动战争，渴望和平，并决心维持和平。与此同时，他却在疯狂地进口飞机和骑兵坦克，以超越邻近的对手。但是没有飞行员，飞机就毫无用处，观察这些督军从哪里获取人员将会很有趣。

张元帅的舰队

据查，张元帅拥有中国最大的空军舰队。他在12月6日收到了40架法国飞机，此前本栏曾对此进行过描述，而路透社错误地报道为12架。当时他拥有约30架可用机器，以及来自意大利的约90台发动机和零部件，因此他实际上拥有一支由60架作战飞机和40架教练机组成的舰队。由于民用航空现已关闭，最后一名留任的英国教官已经离开，但张元帅仍保留着八名俄罗斯飞行员，并正在召集一批新的中国飞行员。他预计将接收六辆小型坦克。

吴佩孚元帅在洛阳拥有约30架可用机器，并有几名优秀的飞行员。

南苑的飞机

曹锟总统在南苑拥有约40架可用机器。其中包括阿弗罗（Avro）、维米（Vimy）和汉德利·佩奇（Handley Page）型飞机。他雇佣了一名美国教官、一名外籍索具工和一名外籍装配工，以及约20名中国飞行员。大约三个月前，曹锟向南京的督军赠送了两架飞机，后者将那里的军事阅兵场改建成了机场。孙博士拥有约11架飞机和一些中国飞行员。另有传闻称，所有这些督军都在疯狂购买卡车底盘以制造装甲车。

何丰林将军的装甲车

何丰林将军拥有25架法国机器和另外两架其他机器，所有这些都已在本栏中描述过。他有一名中国飞行员、两名助理教官和一名外籍飞行员，以及12辆法国骑兵坦克。如果这些督军——笔者特意使用“如果”一词——能够训练飞行员或获得飞行员，那么严重的麻烦将不可避免。在飞行员之间将不存在所谓的中立区。

华盛顿会议与国际联盟一样， remains a nine days' wonder（昙花一现/短暂轰动）。各国政府以一种宏大的姿态，将已建成和在建的战列舰送进了废铁堆。当人们从对这种非凡的自我克制行为的震惊中恢复过来时，他们意识到了其中的犬儒主义。战列舰被报废是因为，面对飞机，它们已经过时且毫无价值。为了消除对此事的任何残留疑虑，可以说，日本目前在飞机上的支出与英国相当。美国也在建立一支庞大的空军舰队，涉及设立2,500名军官和40,000名其他军衔人员。当上述三个国家正在建立世界史上最大的空军部队时，中国 presumably（大概/据推测）正以其支离破碎的方式试图将军事航空建立在坚实的基础上。

上海义勇队（S. V. C.）

然而，我们在这里仍然反应迟钝，如果以上海义勇队（S.V.C.）目前对航空的态度来判断，我们满足于忽视这用惨痛代价学到的教训，甚至在这篇文章墨迹未干之前，我们的装甲车就已经找到了它们的克星。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JANUARY 13, 1924.
AEROPLANES FOR THE S.V.C.
WHY THEY ARE NECESSARY
Artillerymen Blind Without Observation
From Flying Machines
WHAT THE CHINESE TUCHUNS HAVE DONE
By "CONTACT."
The condition of the world to-day indicates that we are as far off as ever from the consummation of the ideal of the League of Nations. It is mainly a question of "policing" the world adequately. The body that is to function under the League of Nations scheme, must not only be the Legislative Chamber for the world, but must also replace national armies by an efficient police force. It is a remarkable thing, but the main arm of such a police force is presented to the world by the mastery of the air, and although the average man has come to look upon the aeroplane as the most deadly instrument of destruction, it might prove to be the most potent instrument in preserving peace between nations.
No Reason For A Scare
To discuss the danger of military aeroplanes in our midst is liable to cause a scare, which the writer certainly does not wish to do. The development of aeroplanes is still in its infancy. One may recall that the principal development in the late war was in motor transport. At the beginning of hostilities France owned 36,000 vehicles suitable for conveyance or service of troops. Four years later this immense fleet had increased four times, and in November 1918 motor transport carried 950,000 men.
These are remarkable figures, indeed, but they fall far short of what it will be possible to achieve in aerial transport. We have machines to-day that are capable of transporting 25 men at 150 m per hour. Imagine how 5,000 such machines could frustrate such a movement as that by which the British reinforced their allies in August, 1914.
In my article last week I described how helpless the modern dreadnought has become against aggression from the air, and I emphatically state that an army without control in the air is an army hopelessly outmatched. One need only point to the Battle of Messines, in June, 1917, when the airmen put 400 enemy batteries out of action in less than six days, enabling our infantry to advance without a single artillery casualty. We know, but always fail to realize, these things. The air service is not an auxiliary arm. It is as separate and distinct in its principal functions as are the Navy and Army.
Wanted: Clear Vision
Here, in the defence scheme of Shanghai, there has been no clear visualization of the respective roles in the future of the sea, land and air forces, or more particularly, of how they will interact with one another, and how they could be welded into one great striking machine, rather than blunder along separately, or completely ignoring the air. There is a total lack of any real grasp of the value of the air in the defence scheme, an entirely new factor in the greater problems of offence and defence.
We shall get nowhere until the full realization of what the possession of aeroplanes in the hands of the Military Tuchuns of China means. Even to-day there is hardly a Tuchun of any importance who has not taken up the study of air aggression, who has not added this new arm to his service, who has not obtained foreign instructors to carry out his scheme. What does it all mean? Are these machines for demonstration only? We are quite sure that they will not be used for Civil aviation or the suppression of bandits, for such schemes have been given very short shrift by these gentlemen. Two of the strongest in the air have, we understand, come to a mutual agreement, whilst the actual Government at Peking has but one machine fit to fly, with no pilots.
These, however, are quite beside the point, since the writer prefers to take them as a species of parable, intended to point out how much more favourably situated for aggressive action any Tuchun will be who has had the prescience to develop his air power.
We imagine that no-one regards seriously the nonsense which was talked until quite lately about there being no more war. One must realize that, so long as human nature and human institutions remain what they are, so long will the ultimate resort for the settlement of disputes be to the force of arms. And China is not different, in this respect, from any other nation.
Security Against Aggression
If, as we must, we accept this as a cardinal article of faith, it follows that we must secure ourselves in Shanghai against aggression from the air, by being prepared to resist it. Our S.V.C. is totally inefficient and blind without it. The defence of the Settlement demands that we have an efficient force, not only against possible street riots, but also a force sufficiently strong to at least protect our women and children and our property. Field guns are useless without observations, and the day of the mounted scout observer is past in China. Therefore, the writer contends that the guns must have aerial observation. How much better is it to know when your enemy is within, say, 100 miles than to wait until he knocks at your door; how much better would it not be to scatter his forces outside the Settlement limits, than wait for the inevitable bloodshed of close range contact. Now, whether we accept these deductions or not, we cannot ignore the fact that the aeroplane places in the hands of an evilly-disposed Tuchun a most potent weapon of offence—not only potent from the destructive point of view, but from that of the appalling suddenness with which it enables him to strike his blow.
Moral Effect
Nothing but the sure and certain knowledge that such a sudden blow will inevitably recoil with violence upon the aggressor will deter such Tuchuns from attempting to meddle with Treaty Ports. The moral is too obvious to need emphasizing, and the writer trusts it will not be lost upon those who direct our military defence policy, or who have their share in moulding that public opinion without which even governments cannot act. The chief complaint is that of restricted vision, which prevents people from seeing any farther ahead than to-morrow—of the probable events of a month hence they have no sense of vision. A defence policy based upon aircraft affords us the only hope of protecting our trade out here.
A Great Question
The question which it seems to the writer requires most to be discussed is: Can the S.V.C. survive against the attack of a single aeroplane? That is the main issue, but there are others which hang to it and must be settled.

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1924年1月13日。
为上海义勇队配备飞机
为何这是必要的
若无飞行器进行观测，炮兵即如盲人
中国督军们已采取的行动
作者：“Contact”

当今世界的局势表明，我们距离实现国际联盟的理想依然遥不可及。这主要是一个如何对世界进行充分“警务治理”的问题。在国际联盟方案下运作的机构，不仅必须成为世界的立法机关，还必须以一支高效的警察部队取代各国军队。值得注意的是，这样一支警察部队的主要力量体现于对制空权的掌握；尽管普通人已将飞机视为最致命的毁灭性武器，但它可能被证明是维护国家间和平的最有力工具。

无需恐慌

讨论我们身边军用飞机的危险可能会引起恐慌，而这正是笔者所不愿看到的。飞机的发展仍处于起步阶段。人们或许记得，上次大战中的主要发展在于机动车运输。战事伊始，法国拥有36,000辆适合运送或服务部队的车辆。四年后，这支庞大的车队增加了四倍，至1918年11月，机动车运输了95万名士兵。

这些数字确实惊人，但与空中运输可能取得的成就相比仍相去甚远。我们今天拥有的机器能够以每小时150英里的速度运送25人。试想一下，如果有5,000架这样的机器，将如何挫败类似1914年8月英国增援其盟友那样的行动。

在上周的文章中，我描述了现代无畏舰在面对空中攻击时变得多么无助，并 emphatically 声明，没有制空权的军队是一支注定处于劣势的军队。只需指出1917年6月的梅西讷战役（Battle of Messines），当时飞行员在不到六天的时间内使400个敌方炮台失去作用，使我军步兵得以在无一炮兵伤亡的情况下推进。我们知道这些事，但总是未能充分认识到。航空服务并非辅助兵种。其主要职能与海军和陆军一样独立且 distinct。

亟需：清晰的视野

在上海的防御方案中，对于海、陆、空军在未来的各自角色，特别是它们如何相互作用，以及如何将它们融合成一台强大的打击机器，而不是各自盲目行动或完全忽视空军，缺乏清晰的构想。对于空气在防御方案中的价值——这是进攻和防御更大问题中的一个全新因素——完全缺乏真正的把握。

除非充分认识到中国军事督军手中拥有飞机意味着什么，否则我们将一事无成。即便在今天，几乎每一位重要的督军都已开始研究空中攻击，都将这一新兵种加入其服役部队，都聘请了外国教官来执行其计划。这一切意味着什么？这些飞机仅用于展示吗？我们可以肯定，它们不会被用于民用航空或剿匪，因为这些计划已被这些绅士们迅速搁置。据我们所知，空中力量最强的两位督军已达成相互协议，而北京的实际政府仅有一架适航飞机，且没有飞行员。

然而，这些都偏离了重点，因为笔者更愿意将其视为一种寓言，旨在指出任何有先见之明发展其空中力量的督军，将在进攻行动中处于多么有利的地位。

我们认为，没有人会认真对待直到最近还在谈论的“不再有战争”的胡言乱语。必须认识到，只要人性和人类制度保持现状，解决争端的最终诉诸手段就将是武力。在这方面，中国与其他任何国家并无不同。

防范侵略的安全

如果我们必须将此作为信仰的核心条款，那么我们就必须通过做好抵抗准备，确保上海免受来自空中的侵略。如果没有飞机，我们的上海义勇队（S.V.C.）将完全无效且如同盲人。租界的防御要求我们拥有一支高效的部队，不仅要应对可能的街头骚乱，还要有一支足够强大的部队，至少能保护我们的妇女、儿童和财产。没有观测，野战炮毫无用处，而在中国，骑马侦察观测员的时代已经过去。因此，笔者主张火炮必须拥有空中观测。若能提前知道敌人尚在例如100英里之外，总比等到他敲你的门要好得多；若能在租界范围外分散其兵力，总比等待近距离接触时不可避免的流血事件要好得多。现在，无论我们是否接受这些推论，我们都不能忽视这样一个事实：飞机将一种极具威力的进攻武器交到了心怀不轨的督军手中——这种威力不仅体现在破坏力上，还体现在它使其能够以惊人的突然性发动打击。

道德效应

只有确信这种突然的打击必然会猛烈地反噬侵略者，才能阻止此类督军试图干涉条约口岸。其道德寓意显而易见，无需强调，笔者希望负责我们军事防御政策的人士，以及在塑造公众舆论方面负有责任的人士（没有公众舆论，甚至政府也无法行动）不要忽视这一点。主要的抱怨是视野受限，这阻碍了人们看得比明天更远——他们对一个月后可能发生的事件缺乏远见。基于飞机的防御政策为我们在这里保护贸易提供了唯一的希望。

一个重大问题

在笔者看来，最需要讨论的问题是：上海义勇队能否在单架飞机的攻击下幸存？这是主要问题，但还有其他与之相关的问题必须解决。

SHANGHAI MERCURY, WEDNESDAY JANUARY. 2, 1924.

DOES SHANGHAI POSSESS AN
AEROPLANE FACTORY?

An Aeroplane That Has Aroused
Much Interest.

IS THERE MYSTERY ATTACHED
TO IT?

Within two hundred yards of the
"Mercury" office there is a completely
equipped aeroplane. It is stored in a
godown where about a dozen mechanics
are busy putting the finishing touches
to the silver gray bird of war. The
question is: "Is this machine purely
a commercial enterprise of some pro-
gressive Chinese, or is it what
the world usually associates aeroplanes
with—a war machine? The machine
would have to be repacked, to be able
to fly out of the godown windows or
out by the large doorway and down
the flight of stone steps into—never
mind the name of the street. That is
for the authorities to discover for
themselves, if they have not done so
already.
Also there is in Shanghai at pre-
sent, a foreigner from Canton. He has
been making enquiries into possible
supplies for the military heads in that
much discussed city. He has been
seeing the builders of this Shanghai
aeroplane, and discovered that his order
could not be executed with the dispatch
necessary to the schemes of the party
requiring six aeroplanes. He was
promised, however, that something
might be done within six months; that
one aeroplane takes two months to
make, and that delivery could not be
depended upon under that time.
In the godown where is stored the
graceful bird of war—or peace! are a
number of what look very much like
engines. They have been seen by a
certain party, and if he does not know
an aeroplane engine, or parts of it,
when he sees one, then his Somme ex-
perience must have warped his vision.
That is quite possible.
Now some time ago a Belgian aviator
came to China, thinking it a progres-
sive place where the commercial side
of flying would be greatly encouraged.
But the eye of Chinese authority
looked askance at him, and informed
him that landing rights were about as
difficult to get in Shanghai as a free
bottle of cabaret champagne. The
Belgian left for Peking to approach
the heads and explain that his pro-
position was not opposed to the peace-
ful instincts of China.
Then there was the case of Major M,
a well-known and highly respected
citizen of Shanghai. He did some
flying, but the strenuous time wasted
in getting the necessary permission
robbed his sport of all its glamour.
So seeing that these two gentlemen
have been unable to perform some
stunts that are purely edifying with-
out being militaristic, it is worthy of
note that the aeroplane that is at pre-
sent in Shanghai should be stored in a
godown of a German firm—or is it a
Swiss firm? The fact that the mention
of Canton does not arouse the blush of
indignation on the faces of the persons
who know all about this aeroplane,
seems to suggest that if there are no
gentlemen desiring an up-to-date com-
mercial vehicle, no very strong objec-
tion would be taken to a suggestion
that the aeroplane two hundred yards
from the "Mercury" office, might be
purchased for a reasonable sum should
the warlords of this arms-hating coun-
try desire a new weapon of attack.
Perhaps the police might look into
the matter, or better still the Bureau
of Economic Affairs could make an
offer for the machine; for after all is
said and done there is no reason why
aeroplanes should not be used as a
business venture. But the mind of
man is always focussed on the suspic-
ious trail. He knows what an aero-
plane can do when supplied with a
number of bombs. Again, we should
like to know if these machines are
still classified in Shanghai, as "arms?"

（批：See Report dated Oct 20 '23 entitled Aviation at Tsinghua.）

《上海信使报》，1924年1月2日，星期三。

上海拥有一家飞机工厂吗？

一架引起极大兴趣的飞机。

其中是否有神秘色彩？

在距《信使报》办公室两百码的地方，有一架装备齐全的飞机。它存放在一家仓库里，大约十二名机械师正忙着为这只银灰色的战争之鸟做最后的修饰。问题是：“这台机器纯粹是一些进取的中国人的商业企业，还是像世界通常将飞机与之联系的那样——一种战争机器？”如果要让这台机器飞出仓库窗户，或者通过大门沿石阶飞入——街道名称无关紧要，就必须重新包装。如果当局尚未发现这一点，那就让他们自己去发现吧。

此外，目前上海有一位来自广州的外国人。他一直在调查为那个备受争议的城市中的军事头目提供可能的补给事宜。他会见了这架上海飞机的制造者，并发现他的订单无法以满足需求方需要六架飞机的计划所需的快速度执行。然而，他得到承诺，六个月内可能会有所进展；制造一架飞机需要两个月，在此时间内无法保证交付。

在这只优雅的战争之鸟——或和平之鸟！——存放的仓库里，有许多看起来非常像发动机的东西。某位人士曾见过它们，如果他在看到飞机发动机或其部件时认不出来，那么他在索姆河（Somme）的经历一定扭曲了他的视力。这完全是有可能的。

不久前，一位比利时飞行员来到中国，认为这是一个进步的地方，飞行的商业方面将受到大力鼓励。但中国当局对他侧目而视，并告知他在上海获得着陆权就像获得一瓶免费的歌舞厅香槟一样困难。这位比利时人前往北京，接触高层并解释他的提议并不违背中国的和平本能。

还有 M 少校的情况，他是上海一位知名且备受尊敬的市民。他进行了一些飞行活动，但获取必要许可所浪费的大量精力剥夺了他这项运动的所有魅力。

因此，鉴于这两位绅士未能完成一些纯粹具有教育意义而非军事性质的特技动作，值得注意的是，目前在上海的这架飞机应存放在一家德国公司——或者是瑞士公司？——的仓库里。提到广州并未在那些了解这架飞机全部内情的人脸上激起愤怒的红晕，这一事实似乎表明，如果没有绅士想要一辆最新的商用车辆，那么对于这个厌恶武器的国家的军阀们若想购买一种新的攻击武器，以合理的价格购买这架距《信使报》办公室两百码的飞机，也不会有太强烈的反对意见。

也许警方可以调查此事，或者更好的是，经济事务局可以为这台机器出价；毕竟，没有理由不将飞机用作商业冒险。但人们的思想总是集中在可疑的线索上。他知道当飞机配备一定数量的炸弹时能做什么。此外，我们想知道这些机器在上海是否仍被归类为“武器”？

（批注：参见题为《清华的航空》的1923年10月20日报告。）

CONFIDENTIAL.

My dear Barton,

It has been ascertained that a consignment of aeroplanes, ordered from France by Tupan Lu Yung-hiong of Chekiang, arrived here on November 21 by the Chinese warship "Chaowu". The cargo was discharged at the pontoons at the Arsenal and later conveyed to Lunghua in motor trucks. Inquiries go to show that the aeroplanes were brought by the steamer "Hwa Kung", belonging to the Yue Fong Steamship Company, from Indo-China to Haimung, Tsungming, where they were transferred to the "Chaowu". In addition to the consignment of aeroplanes, the "Chaowu" is reported to have brought to Shanghai Lieutenant Chu, the Chinese aviator, and Dr. Tartois, a representative of Chapeau Freres, the French firm which made the deal for the purchase of the machines. Dr. Tartois is said to have visited Saigon or Haiphong for the purpose of supervising transhipment. The exact number of aeroplanes in the consignment has not yet been ascertained, but according to a report from a well informed source, there are eight large and two small machines, and the cargo in addition includes an armoured automobile.

Yours sincerely,

S. Barton, Esquire, C. M. G.
H. B. M.'s Consul-General,
Shanghai.

Work in the aerodrome at Loonghua has been
suspended since September 12 when a German named
Schottler, who was in charge, was dismissed on
the plea that he was incompetent.
Lieutenant Tsu, who was in the French Flying
Corps during the war, is a son of Nicolas Tsu,
Compradore of the Banque de l'Indo-Chine. Enquiries
have failed to elicit any information that either
he or his father has been in the service of the
Government at Peking, but both are undoubtedly
friendly with many highly placed officials. The
family has been very reticent about the business
that took young Tsu to France. There is, however,
reason to believe that the story that he went there
for aeroplanes is true. An informant has stated
that he knows that a ship has been irregularly
chartered to convey the machines from a point on
the Southern coast of China to their destination
which is understood to be Chekiang. This man
declined to give further particulars at present
but promised to do so on October 27, by which date
the conspirators apparently hope to have the
aeroplanes safely delivered. Arrangements are now
being made for the purchase on behalf of Chang Tso
Ling of fifty more flying machines from the same
parties. Lieut. Tsu has not yet returned to
Shanghai, but is expected back before the end of
October, 1923.
Since his dismissal from Loonghua Schottler
and three of the mechanics, who worked with him
there, have been employed repairing aeroplane parts
in No. 10A Hongkong Road, a godown belonging to Buckleib & Co.

朱中尉(Lieutenant Tsu)曾在战争期间服役于法国飞行队，他是东方汇理银行(Banque de l'Indo-Chine)买办朱葆三(Nicolas Tsu)的儿子。调查未能获得任何表明他或其父亲曾在北京政府任职的信息，但两人无疑与许多高官关系友好。该家族对让小朱去法国做生意一事非常缄默。然而，有理由相信他去那里是为了飞机的说法是真实的。一名线人表示，他知道有一艘船被非正式地租用，用于将机器从中国南部沿海的一个地点运往目的地，据悉目的地是浙江。此人目前拒绝提供更多细节，但承诺在10月27日提供，届时阴谋者显然希望飞机已安全送达。目前正安排代表张作霖(Chang Tso Ling)从同一方购买另外五十架飞行器。朱中尉尚未返回上海，但预计将于1923年10月底前回来。

Enquiries regarding the Shanghai Portland
Cement Co. indicate that it is purely a
Chinese concern entirely free from German
control. The directors include Mr. Chu Pao

silk merchant. Mr. Lieu Ong Sung is the
moving spirit of the enterprise and occupies
the post of Managing Director. The machinery

be an exact model of that in use in the

found of the report that the machinery is of
such a type that the factory could be easily
converted into a powder making plant. In fact,
all the information reaching the police tend to

关于上海波特兰水泥公司（Shanghai Portland Cement Co.）的调查显示，该公司纯属华商企业，完全不受德国人控制。董事包括前上海总商会会长朱葆三先生、南通实业巨子张謇先生、其弟张詧先生、商务印书馆经理李拔可先生、著名学者兼实业倡导者李维格博士、著名工程与建筑承包商同名商号负责人张允来先生、煤商兼银行家杜嘉坤先生、招商局轮船公司的谢先生、著名丝商杨宽候先生。刘鸿声先生是该企业的核心人物，担任总经理一职。据称，从瑞士进口的机器是霍尔班克（Holderbank）工厂所用机器的精确复制品，但无法证实有关该机器类型可使工厂轻易转产为火药制造厂的说法。事实上，警方掌握的所有信息都倾向于否定这一说法。

Arrangements are now being made for the purchase on behalf of Chang Tso Ling (張作霖) of fifty more flying machines from the same parties. Lieut. Tsu has not yet returned to Shanghai, but is expected back before the end of October 1923.

Since his dismissal from Lunghua Schottler and three of the mechanics, who worked with him there, have been employed repairing aeroplane parts in No. 10A Hongkong Road, a godown belonging to Buchheister & Co.

AVIATION LOONGHWA

The following information is considered reliable:-

The two seater machine which was tested last month was a success. The machine is practically a copy of a Bristol Two Seater and is considered excellent.

Weight empty 1,600 lbs; weight loaded 3,000 lbs; Speed 120 H.P.H.; climbs to 10,000 feet in thirteen minutes. Its normal endurance in the air is four hours, but with an additional tank its endurance is increased to eight hours.

The report that there are eighteen more engines at LOONGHWA is not confirmed. It is definitely stated that there are not more than ten there at present. Of these ten, six are British and four are German. The types are:- A.W., Beardmore, Daimler, and three Lorraine.

These engines are reported to have been in the country a couple of years.

All the instruments came from or through a firm called SMITH in LONDON.

All material for the construction of machines, except engines and instruments, can now be provided and manufactured in CHINA. The difficulty of obtaining suitable wood has been overcome. The Germans have found wood in CHINA (place unknown) that is suitable for Propellers and Fusilage. These woods were used in the two seater in place of Spruce and Ash.

There are now on the stocks, 1 Single Seater, 4 Two Seater, and 6 Six Seater Passenger machines.

上个月测试的双座机取得了成功。该机器实际上是布里斯托尔双座机的复制品，被认为性能优异。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 18, 1923.

SHANGHAI CEMENT
FACTORY

An Important Local Industrial
Enterprise: Shanghai Port-
land Cement Works Ld.

Perhaps only those who are
directly interested have been
aware that during the last 16
months a very important in-
dustrial plant has been under
construction on the banks of
the Huangpu, above the Kiang-
nan Dock, which will aid
further in keeping Shanghai
the most important industrial
city in the Far East. Holiday-
makers going up the river
on their house-boat trips and pas-
sing Lunghua, have noticed two
queer-looking cement reinforced
chimneys, which are the stacks of
the Shanghai Portland Cement
Works, Ld. The firm have just
completed their buildings and
the erection of machinery for the
manufacture of their Elephant
Brand Portland cement in Shang-
hai to meet the enormous local
demand, as well as for export.
For one who has had no previous
knowledge of the existence of this
large cement factory, it is indeed
a pleasant surprise to find that it
has been put up quietly and is,
judging from what one was able
to gather during a short visit, one
of the most up-to-date plants of
its kind in the East.

The works cover an area of
about 200 mow of land, with an
excellent water frontage of over
1,200 feet. The factory buildings
are of reinforced concrete with
solid cement block foundation.
The chimneys also are built of
cement reinforced concrete--a type
of construction entirely new in
this part of the East. The office
buildings, as well as the residen-
ces and staff quarters, are of
modern type. There are spacious
godowns already packed full with
stores of a thousand and one
descriptions. The barrel factory,
where barrels are made for hold-
ing cement, is another interest-
ing place. Here one can see a big
log of wood being converted into
grooved staves and tops in a sur-
prisingly short space of time.
The silo, or cement store, is only
partly finished and, according to
the plan, when finished it will
look more like an ancient Baby-
lonian structure than a compara-
tively newly conceived design for
storing cement for the purpose of
of "ageing" or keeping it from
deterioration. There are two
wharves with ample accommoda-
tion for landing coal and raw
materials such as limestone, clay
and gypsum. The wharf for
landing stone, etc., is installed
with a new type of crane specially
adapted for lifting limestone and
clay from native boats. Alongside
the wharves are tons and tons of
limestone and clay lying in boats
ready to be unloaded. They are
sent from Huchow and Sungkiang,
where the works have their own
quarries. The officials of the
works spoke with unconcealed
pleasure with regard to the
quality of their raw materials ob-
tained from these localities. One
observed that they did not expect
any undue competition in this
trade, as the demand for cement
exceeds the supply.

A Big Daily Output.

The cement machinery was de-
signed and made by the well
known cement machinery makers,
Messrs. G. Polysius, of Dessau,
under the personal supervision of
the works' engineer-in-chief, Mr.
H. Mollitor, formerly engineer-in-
chief of the Hupch Cement Works
The machinery is of the rotary
type, with a guaranteed output
of 1,200 casks of 375 lb. nett per
day. The method used is the wet
process, which produces under
equal conditions a better grade
of cement than the dry process,
owing to the uniform mixture of
raw materials obtainable there-
with. The machinery has all the
latest labour-saving devices which
will eliminate as far as possible
the human factor. The works
have their own power plant, a
turbo-generator unit 1,500 k.w.,
500 volts, manufactured and in-
stalled by the Siemens-Schuckert
Works. A separate unit is also in-
stalled for lighting the whole of
the works, with a 100 h.p. Diesel
engine using crude oil. Both the
water installation and drainage
system show that the works have
left out nothing which would make
the plant completely equipped.

Purely Chinese.

In a short time the Shanghai
Portland Cement Works expect to
put on the market their product
the "Elephant" brand cement and
by the time the first cask is sent
out the company will have invested
in this new Shanghai industry a
capital of $2,500,000. The Com-
pany is capitalized and managed
entirely by Chinese, although for
its best interest the technical side
of the manufacturing has been en-
trusted to a foreign expert. The
list of directors contains the
names of such well-known merch-
ants as Mr. Chu Pao-san, former
Chairman of the Chinese General
Chamber of Commerce, Mr. Chang
Chien, the Nantungchow industri-
al magnate, and his brother, Mr.
Chang Char, Mr. Li Pah-koh,
manager of the Commercial Press,
Dr. V. K. Lee, a well-known
scholar and promoter of industr-
ies, Mr. Y. L. Chang, head of the
famous firm of engineers and con-
tractors and of the Kow Kee
Lumber Co., Mr. Du Chia-quan,
coal merchant and banker, Mr.
Zia, of the China Merchants, Mr.
K. E. Yang, a well known silk
merchant and others. Mr. Lieu
Ong-sung is the moving spirit
of the whole enterprise and
is the managing director. Besides
being interested in numerous other
industrial enterprises he has
devoted a great deal of his thought
and attention to making the ex-
istence of a cement factory in the
vicinity of Shanghai an accom-
plished fact. Throughout the or-
ganization of the company and the
construction of the works, Mr.
Lieu has been ably assisted tech-
nically by Mr. Mollitor, who is

上海水泥厂

一家重要的本地工业企业：上海波特兰水泥有限公司

或许只有那些直接感兴趣的人才知道，在过去16个月里，一座非常重要的工业设施一直在黄浦江畔、江南船坞上游处进行建设，这将进一步助力上海保持其作为远东最重要工业城市的地位。乘坐游艇沿河而上度假并经过龙华的人们，已经注意到两座外形奇特的钢筋混凝土烟囱，那便是上海波特兰水泥有限公司的烟筒。该公司刚刚完成了厂房建设以及用于生产“象牌”波特兰水泥的机器安装，以满足巨大的本地需求及出口需要。对于此前不知晓这家大型水泥厂存在的人来说，发现它已悄然建成，并且根据短暂参观所了解的情况判断，它是东方同类工厂中最为现代化的工厂之一，这确实是一个令人愉快的惊喜。

该厂占地约200亩，拥有超过1,200英尺的优质临水岸线。厂房建筑采用钢筋混凝土结构，地基为坚固的水泥砌块。烟囱也由钢筋混凝土建造——这种建筑结构在东亚地区尚属全新类型。办公大楼以及住宅和员工宿舍均为现代风格。宽敞的仓库里已经堆满了各种各样的存货。制造用于盛装水泥的木桶的桶厂是另一个有趣的地方。在这里，人们可以看到一根巨大的原木在极短的时间内被加工成带槽的桶板和桶盖。筒仓（即水泥储存库）仅部分完工，按照计划，完工后它看起来更像是一座古老的巴比伦建筑，而不是一个相对新颖的、旨在通过“陈化”或防止变质来储存水泥的设计。这里有两个码头，拥有充足的空间用于卸载煤炭以及石灰石、粘土和石膏等原材料。用于卸载石块等的码头配备了一种新型起重机，专门适用于从民船上吊运石灰石和粘土。码头旁停泊着装载着成吨石灰石和粘土的船只，准备卸货。这些原料来自湖州和松江，公司在这些地方拥有自己的采石场。厂方官员毫不掩饰地表达了对从这些地方获得的原材料质量的满意之情。有人指出，他们不指望在这一行业出现任何过度的竞争，因为水泥的需求量超过了供应量。

巨大的日产量。

水泥机械由德绍（Dessau）著名的水泥机械制造商G. Polysius公司设计和制造，并在该厂总工程师H. Mollitor先生（前华新水泥厂总工程师）的个人监督下完成。该机械为回转窑类型，保证日产量为1,200桶，每桶净重375磅。所采用的方法是湿法工艺，由于由此可获得均匀的原料混合，因此在同等条件下，湿法工艺生产的水泥等级优于干法工艺。该机械配备了所有最新的省力装置，将尽可能消除人为因素。工厂拥有自己的发电厂，包括一台由西门子-舒克特工厂（Siemens-Schuckert Works）制造和安装的1,500千瓦、500伏涡轮发电机组。此外还安装了一个独立的单元用于整个工厂的照明，配备一台使用原油的100马力柴油发动机。供水设施和排水系统均表明，工厂在使设备完全配套方面没有遗漏任何环节。

纯华商办。

上海波特兰水泥有限公司预计将在短时间内将其产品“象牌”水泥投放市场，而在第一桶水泥发出之时，公司将在这项新的上海产业中投入资本250万美元。该公司的资本构成和管理完全由华人负责，尽管为了公司的最大利益，制造方面的技术工作已委托给一位外国专家。董事名单中包含一些著名商人的名字，如前上海总商会会长朱葆三先生、南通实业巨子张謇先生及其弟张詧先生、商务印书馆经理李拔可先生、著名学者兼实业促进者李登辉博士、著名工程承包商及久记木业公司负责人张裕光先生、煤商兼银行家杜家坤先生、招商局的谢先生、著名丝商杨凯之先生等。刘鸿生先生是整个企业的推动者，并担任总经理。除了对众多其他工业企业感兴趣外，他还投入了大量的思考和精力，使在上海附近建立一家水泥厂成为既成事实。在整个公司组织和工厂建设过程中，刘先生在技术方面得到了Mollitor先生的得力协助，Mollitor先生负责……（原文此处似乎有OCR错误或残缺，结合上下文应指负责全厂的技术工作）。

Extract from Daily Report
KOREA
of December 12, 1928

It is reported that the Military Authorities
at Lunghua intend to strengthen the local garrison
by the addition of an air section which for the
present will consist of five aeroplanes. One of these,
an "Avro", which was purchased from the Central Garage,
is already fit for use, and the four others which
have "Daimler" engines are being overhauled. The
work is being done by a German named F. Schoettler
who has about twenty Chinese carpenters and mechanics
under his control. Local foreigners interested in
flying claim that the Lunghua Military Authorities
have in their possession between twenty and thirty
aeroplanes and seventy five spare engines, but no
corroboration of those reports could be obtained from
Chinese sources.
